name: Advayatāraka: targets, voids and tāraka

stages.name: antar-lakṣya
stages.description: Kuṇḍalinī in the suṣumnā; the inner sound; blue light between the eyes.

stages.name: bahir-lakṣya
stages.description: Colours of space before the nose; rays; the light above the head.

stages.name: guṇa-rahita ākāśa
stages.description: First void of the intermediate target.

stages.name: paramākāśa
stages.description: Like dense darkness lit by stars.

stages.name: mahākāśa
stages.description: Like the fire of dissolution.

stages.name: tattvākāśa
stages.description: Brilliant beyond compare.

stages.name: sūryākāśa
stages.description: Like crores of suns.

stages.name: amanaska (uttara-tāraka)
stages.description: The later tāraka, beyond mind.

name: The four yogas of the Amaraughaprabodha

stages.name: mantra-yoga
stages.description: Repetition of mantra.

stages.name: laya-yoga
stages.description: Dissolution of the mind, as in the inner sound.

stages.name: haṭha-yoga
stages.description: The great seal, great lock and great piercing, as means.

stages.name: rāja-yoga
stages.description: The goal to which the others lead.

notes: The four are enumerated rather than strictly sequential; compare pth:dattatreya-four-yogas (U51).

name: Amṛtanāda: the six-limbed yoga

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Withdrawing the senses and mind from objects.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation (listed second in this text).

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Exhalation, inhalation, retention with the praṇava; burns faults.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Holding the mind in the Self.

stages.name: tarka
stages.description: Reasoning not opposed to the āgamas.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: That by which, attained, all is regarded as equal; kaivalya in six months.

name: The fifteen limbs of the Aparokṣānubhūti (pañcadaśāṅga-yoga)

stages.name: yama
stages.description: control of the senses through knowing 'all is Brahman'

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: constant flow of like thoughts (of Brahman), excluding others

stages.name: tyāga
stages.description: abandoning the world of appearances by seeing it as consciousness

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: that from which words turn back: abiding in it

stages.name: deśa
stages.description: the 'place' where there is no people at beginning, middle or end — Brahman

stages.name: kāla
stages.description: the indivisible Brahman in which all time arises

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: that in which one can meditate on Brahman uninterruptedly with ease

stages.name: mūla-bandha
stages.description: Brahman, the root of all beings, in which the mind is restrained

stages.name: deha-sāmya
stages.description: absorption in the uniform Brahman, not mere straightness of body

stages.name: dṛk-sthiti
stages.description: seeing the world as Brahman, not gazing at the nose-tip

stages.name: prāṇa-saṃyamana
stages.description: negation of the world (exhalation), 'I am Brahman' (inhalation), steadiness in it (retention)

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: seeing the self in all objects, merging the mind in consciousness

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: holding the mind on Brahman wherever it goes

stages.name: ātma-dhyāna
stages.description: the unsupported state 'I am Brahman alone'

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: the mode's changeless, distinction-free identity with Brahman, forgetting all modes

notes: Order and glosses from memory (moderate); verse numbers low. The text says haṭha-yoga combined with this is for the unripe; for the ripe this alone suffices (vv. c. 143–144). Bands are interpretive.

name: From the yoga of understanding to brahmanirvāṇa (BhG 2.39–72)

stages.name: buddhiyoga in action
stages.gloss: acting established in yoga, attachment abandoned, the same in success and failure
stages.description: The understanding 'according to yoga' (2.39): entitlement to action and not its fruit; equanimity is yoga, yoga is skill in actions; the fruit abandoned, one is freed from the bondage of birth (2.47–51).

stages.name: crossing the thicket of delusion
stages.description: When the understanding crosses the thicket of delusion, one becomes indifferent to what is to be heard and what has been heard (2.52).

stages.name: attaining yoga
stages.description: When the understanding, perplexed by what it has heard, stands unwavering and immovable in samādhi, one attains yoga (2.53).

stages.name: sthitaprajña
stages.description: All desires given up, content in the self by the self; senses withdrawn; unshaken in pain and pleasure; free of 'mine' and 'I'; serenity and peace (2.55–71).

stages.name: brāhmī sthiti and brahmanirvāṇa
stages.gloss: the state of brahman; its nirvāṇa at death
stages.description: Having attained the brāhmī sthiti one is no longer deluded; abiding in it even at death one attains brahmanirvāṇa (2.72).

notes: The order of stages 1–3 follows the text's own 'when … then' clauses (2.52–53); stage 4 answers Arjuna's question at 2.54, and stage 5 is named at 2.72. The Gītā does not itself present these as a numbered ladder. Bands belong to the interpretation layer and are given only where the fit seemed clear.

name: The heart-lotus meditation taught to Uddhava (BhP 11.14.32-46)

stages.name: sama āsana, breath
stages.gloss: posture, gaze, purification of the breath-channels

stages.name: heart-lotus visualisation
stages.gloss: lotus, sun-moon-fire, the Lord's form in the fire

stages.name: pratyāhāra with buddhi as charioteer
stages.gloss: senses withdrawn, mind led to the Lord

stages.name: one point: the smile
stages.gloss: the whole form gathered to the smiling face

stages.name: space, then nothing
stages.gloss: mind fixed in space, then no thought

stages.name: jyotir jyotiṣi
stages.gloss: the self seen in the Lord, light in light

stages.name: nirvāṇa of the triple delusion
stages.gloss: delusion of object, knowledge, action at rest

name: The yogin's gradual ascent after death (BhP 2.2.22-31)

stages.name: Vaiśvānara
stages.description: purified, he reaches Agni

stages.name: the world of the wise for a kalpa (Maharloka)
Satyaloka (pārameṣṭhya)
stages.description: reached when the universe burns

stages.name: passage through the elements, senses, mind and vijñāna

notes: A post-mortem ascent rather than a stage-map of practice; only the final stage is banded.

name: The Bhāgavata's sequence from hearing to seeing the Lord (BhP 1.2.16-21)

stages.name: mahat-sevā, tīrtha-niṣevaṇa
stages.gloss: service of great souls and holy places
stages.description: Serving the great and holy places gives faith and the wish to hear.

stages.name: kathā-ruci
stages.description: A taste for hearing the Lord's stories arises.

stages.name: abhadra-vidhūnana
stages.description: Kṛṣṇa in the heart of the hearer removes impurities.

stages.name: naiṣṭhikī bhakti
stages.description: With impurities almost gone, by service to the Bhāgavata, steady devotion arises.

stages.name: sattve prasāda
stages.description: The mind, untouched by rajas, tamas, lust and greed, rests in sattva and becomes clear.

stages.name: bhagavat-tattva-vijñāna
stages.gloss: knowledge of the reality of Bhagavān
stages.description: To the clear, unattached mind knowledge of the Lord's reality arises.

stages.name: hṛdaya-granthi-bheda
stages.gloss: the knot of the heart cut
stages.description: Seeing the Lord as the self, the heart's knot is cut, doubts severed, karmas exhausted.

name: Bhṛgu's five realizations (TU 3)
description: Seeking brahman by tapas, as defined by Varuṇa (that from which beings arise, live and return), Bhṛgu understands brahman successively as food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss (cf. the five selves of TU 2).

stages.name: annaṃ brahma
stages.description: Understood by tapas; returns to Varuṇa.

stages.name: ānando brahma
stages.description: The knowledge of Bhṛgu and Varuṇa, established in the highest heaven.

stages.name: the knower's song
stages.gloss: moving through the worlds singing 'I am food'
stages.description: Having passed into the five selves, the knower moves through the worlds eating what he wishes and taking what form he wishes, singing.

notes: Stages 1-4 are successive understandings within one inquiry; bands assigned only to the last two.

name: Sanatkumāra's ladder to plenitude (ChU 7)
description: Nārada is led from name, through fourteen ever greater objects of veneration up to breath, then through a chain of conditions from truth to happiness, to plenitude and the self.

stages.name: nāma
stages.description: Venerate name as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: vāc
stages.description: Venerate speech as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: manas
stages.description: Venerate mind as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: saṅkalpa
stages.description: Venerate intention as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: citta
stages.description: Venerate thought as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Venerate meditation as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: vijñāna
stages.description: Venerate understanding as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: bala
stages.description: Venerate strength as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: anna
stages.description: Venerate food as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: āpas
stages.description: Venerate water as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: tejas
stages.description: Venerate heat as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: ākāśa
stages.description: Venerate space as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: smara
stages.description: Venerate memory as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: āśā
stages.description: Venerate hope as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: prāṇa
stages.description: Venerate breath as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: satya
stages.description: Truth must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: vijñāna
stages.description: Understanding must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: mati
stages.description: Reflection must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: Faith must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: niṣṭhā
stages.description: Steadfastness must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: kṛti
stages.description: Action must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: sukha
stages.description: Happiness must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: bhūman
stages.description: Where one sees, hears, understands nothing else: happiness, the immortal.

stages.name: ahaṃkārādeśa / ātmādeśa
stages.gloss: the teaching of 'I' and of the self
stages.description: Plenitude is all; I am all; the self is all; one who sees thus delights in the self and is self-ruled (svarāj); the knots are loosened and he is shown the far shore beyond darkness.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer: the fifteen rungs are meditative venerations (B2); the chain 16-22 is a regress of conditions, not a practice sequence, so no band is assigned.

name: Darśana: the eight-limbed yoga

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Ten restraints.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Ten observances.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Named postures.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Breath-regulation (counts not reproduced).

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Five kinds of withdrawal.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Concentration.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation with or without qualities.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Knowledge of the unity of jīva and the supreme.

name: The four conditions of the Dāsbodh (baddha, mumukṣu, sādhaka, siddha)

stages.name: baddha
stages.description: Sunk in worldly pleasures and possessions, without thought of the Self.

stages.name: mumukṣu
stages.description: Disgusted with worldly life, longing for freedom, seeking the company of the good.

stages.name: sādhaka
stages.description: Takes up hearing, reflection and devotion under the guru, disciplining conduct.

stages.name: siddha
stages.description: Abides in the Self, free of doubt, while continuing right action in the world.

notes: The sādhaka stage spans bands B2–B6 in practice; siddha's continued action also touches B8.

name: The path of the gods (arcirādi-mārga) in the Brahma Sūtras

stages.name: utkrānti
stages.description: speech merges in mind, mind in breath, breath in the self; the meditator departs by the channel beyond the hundred (crown)

stages.name: arcis
stages.description: first station of the path, 'that being well known'

stages.name: ahar, śukla-pakṣa, uttarāyaṇa, saṃvatsara
stages.gloss: day, bright fortnight, northern course, year
stages.description: stations of the path (listed in the Upaniṣads; ordered by BS 4.3.2–3)

stages.name: vāyu, āditya, candra, vidyut
stages.description: further stations; the stations are deities who conduct the soul (ātivāhika)

stages.name: amānava puruṣa (with Varuṇa, Indra, Prajāpati)
stages.description: from lightning a non-human person leads the soul on to Brahman

stages.name: brahmaloka
stages.description: for Bādari and Śaṅkara, the conditioned Brahman

stages.name: kāryātyaye mokṣa
stages.gloss: liberation at the dissolution of that world
stages.description: with its ruler, beyond it; no return

notes: An eschatological route rather than a meditative ladder; bands left empty for the stations. Station order recalled with moderate confidence. Advaita: this path is only for meditators on the qualified Brahman; the knower of the attributeless does not depart.

name: Dhyānabindu / Yogacūḍāmaṇi: the six-limbed yoga

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Siddha, bhadra, siṃha, padma; posture destroys disease.

stages.name: prāṇasaṃrodha
stages.description: Breath-control destroys sin.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Withdrawal removes mental disturbance.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Gives steadiness of mind.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation on Oṃ / the Self.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Gives the wonderful consciousness and liberation.

name: From direct knowledge to liberation (Dvaita)

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: The knower sees the Lord (as fitness allows); acquired karma no longer binds.

stages.name: prārabdha-bhoga
stages.description: The knower remains embodied until the karma in effect is spent.

stages.name: utkrānti
stages.description: At death the tip of the heart lights up and the knower leaves by the crown channel, helped by Hari in the heart; some are liberated without departing.

stages.name: arcirādi-mārga
stages.description: The knower goes by the path of light to Brahmā's world.

stages.name: brahmaṇā saha mokṣa
stages.description: At the great dissolution those in Brahmā's world reach the Supreme together with Brahmā.

stages.name: mukti-bhoga
stages.description: Sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya or sāyujya; bliss graded a hundredfold by class; desires in accord with the Lord's; bhakti continuing as eternal bliss.

notes: Assembled from Madhva's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 3–4; the order of stages follows the sūtras. Bands are interpretive; B8 for prārabdha-bhoga is a correspondence of position only — Dvaita does not treat the embodied knower as already liberated in the sense of final mokṣa.

name: The Dvaita sequence of means (sādhana-krama)

stages.name: adhikāra, vairāgya
stages.description: Eligibility by nature, class and qualities; for the highest, dispassion that sees everything from Brahmā to a blade of grass as worthless and impermanent, and sole refuge in Viṣṇu.

stages.name: sadācāra, niṣkāma-karma
stages.description: Prescribed duties done without desire and offered to Hari as the real doer; vows such as Ekādaśī.

stages.name: guru-upasatti, dīkṣā
stages.description: Gaining the supreme knowledge from the grace of a teacher; initiation into Hari's worship.

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: Study of the true scriptures with Madhva's commentaries.

stages.name: manana
stages.description: Reasoned reflection removing doubts.

stages.name: dhyāna / nididhyāsana, upāsanā
stages.description: Meditation on Hari with qualities fit for the meditator, within the heart as one's original (bimba).

stages.name: bhakti
stages.gloss: devotion grounded in knowledge of God's greatness
stages.description: Firm love exceeding all other love; accompanies and crowns every stage.

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: Direct realization of the Lord, as fitness allows; the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived.

stages.name: paramātma-prasāda
stages.description: Won by fullness of knowledge; without it there is no liberation.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Release into one's own bliss in the Lord's presence (see pth:dvaita-moksa-krama).

notes: A composite ordering of means that Madhva and the tradition name in several places (BSB 1.1.1; MBTN 1.85–99; Nyāyāmṛta 3; Yogadīpikā 1). The texts do not give this exact ten-step list; the sequence and the bands are the interpretation layer. Bhakti and grace are not a single 'stage' for the tradition: bhakti accompanies every step, and grace alone liberates.

name: The four orders of life in sequence (Manu)

stages.name: upanayana
stages.description: Entry into Vedic study with the Sāvitrī (MDh 2.36, 2.169–171).

stages.name: brahmacarya
stages.description: Study of the Veda in the teacher's house, chastity, service, sense-restraint (MDh 2; 3.1–2).

stages.name: gārhasthya
stages.description: Marriage, the five great sacrifices, the debts to gods, seers and ancestors, livelihood by one's dharma (MDh 3–5).

stages.name: vānaprasthya
stages.description: Withdrawal to the forest with austerities, study of the Upaniṣads and daily rites (MDh 6.1–32).

stages.name: saṃnyāsa / parivrājya
stages.description: Depositing the fires in oneself, wandering alone, breath-control, fixation, withdrawal and meditation, seeing the self in all (MDh 6.33–85).

stages.name: brahmaṇy avasthāna
stages.description: Freed from all pairs of opposites, he abides in Brahman; one with right vision is not bound by actions (MDh 6.74, 6.81).

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer claims (logged). Other texts allow the orders as options or recognize only the householder (dsp:asrama-vikalpa-samuccaya-badha).

name: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā: the six samādhis (parallel routes)

stages.name: bhakti-yoga samādhi
stages.gloss: by devotion to the chosen deity

stages.name: manomūrcchā samādhi
stages.gloss: by the swoon of the mind

notes: NOT a sequence: six alternative routes to the one samādhi that the GS calls rājayoga and 'the mark of liberation' (7.17). 'order' is the text's order of exposition only. All banded B4 (absorption), with the text's claim of liberation (B7) noted. Verse refs of 7.7–16 recalled from structure.

name: The ascent in yoga of BhG ch. 6

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is the means (6.3).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.description: When attached neither to objects nor to actions and having renounced all intentions, one has ascended; quiescence is then the means (6.2–4).

stages.name: dhyāna practice
stages.description: Seated firmly, erect, gaze controlled, the mind is made one-pointed, stilled by degrees and brought back whenever it wanders; it becomes steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.10–26).

stages.name: brahma-saṃsparśa
stages.description: The calm yogin attains the endless happiness of contact with Brahman and sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.27–29).

stages.name: seeing the Lord everywhere
stages.description: He sees the Lord everywhere and everything in him, worships him abiding in all beings, and regards others' pleasure and pain as his own (6.30–32).

stages.name: peace culminating in nirvāṇa
stages.description: The yogin attains the peace that culminates in nirvāṇa and abides in the Lord (6.15); of all yogins the one who worships him with faith is the most yoked (6.47).

notes: If the yogin falls short, the effort is carried into a later birth (6.40–45).

name: The graded devotional practices of BhG 12.8–12

stages.name: karmaphala-tyāga
stages.gloss: relinquishing the fruit of all actions
stages.description: If one cannot do even the Lord's work, then, taking refuge in his yoga and self-controlled, give up the fruit of all actions (12.11).

stages.name: mat-karma-parama
stages.gloss: being intent on the Lord's work
stages.description: If one cannot practise, be intent on doing actions for the Lord's sake; even so one attains perfection (12.10).

stages.name: abhyāsa-yoga
stages.description: If one cannot fix the mind steadily, seek to reach the Lord by the yoga of practice (12.9).

stages.name: fixing mind and intellect on the Lord
stages.description: Fix your mind on the Lord alone and rest your intellect in him (12.8).

stages.name: dwelling in the Lord
stages.description: Thereafter you will dwell in him (12.8).

notes: The text presents the steps from the highest downward as alternatives by capacity; they are listed here from the most accessible upward. 12.12 gives a different ranking (practice < knowledge < meditation < relinquishing the fruit, from which peace follows); commentators reconcile the two differently.

name: From one's own work to entering the Lord (BhG 18.45–56)

stages.name: svakarma as worship
stages.gloss: worshipping the Lord by one's own work
stages.description: Each devoted to his own work attains perfection by worshipping with it him from whom beings arise (18.45–46).

stages.name: naiṣkarmya-siddhi
stages.gloss: the perfection of freedom from action
stages.description: With intellect unattached everywhere, self-conquered, free of longing, one attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action (18.49).

stages.name: dhyāna-yoga and fitness for Brahman
stages.description: With purified intellect, restraint, solitude, light food, controlled speech, body and mind, constant meditation, dispassion, and the giving up of ego, force, pride, desire, anger and possession, one becomes fit for becoming Brahman (18.50–53).

stages.name: brahmabhūta
stages.description: Having become Brahman, serene, one neither grieves nor desires and is the same to all beings (18.54).

stages.name: parā bhakti
stages.description: He attains supreme devotion to the Lord, and by devotion knows him in truth (18.54–55).

stages.name: entering the Lord; the eternal abode
stages.description: Knowing him in truth he enters him; even while doing all actions, taking refuge in him, by his grace he attains the eternal, imperishable abode (18.55–56).

notes: Stage order is the text's; the bands are the interpretation layer. Commentators differ on whether knowledge (Advaita) or devotion (Vaiṣṇava) is the final stage — see dsp:gita-primary-teaching.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Gorakṣaśataka

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Siddhāsana and padmāsana, the two pre-eminent of the eighty-four; posture destroys disease (GŚ 5–9, 54).

stages.name: prāṇasaṃyāma
stages.description: Alternate breathing through moon and sun with the five seals; it burns sin; signs of sweat, trembling, rising (GŚ 32–53).

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The sun draws in the moon's nectar; withdrawal removes mental disturbance (GŚ 54–66).

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Holding the mind on the five elements in heart, throat, palate, brows and brahmarandhra (GŚ 67–75).

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation with qualities on the centres and without qualities on Śiva and the all-pervading self (GŚ 76–93).

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: The samarasa oneness when breath is exhausted and mind dissolved; beyond time and karma; non-duality in the supreme state like milk in milk (GŚ 94–101).

name: Haṃsa: the ten inner sounds

stages.name: ciṇī
stages.description: Sound 1; effect: tingling.

stages.name: ciñciṇī
stages.description: Sound 2; effect: limbs 'break'.

stages.name: ghaṇṭā (bell)
stages.description: Sound 3; effect: fatigue.

stages.name: śaṅkha (conch)
stages.description: Sound 4; effect: head shakes.

stages.name: tantrī (lute)
stages.description: Sound 5; effect: palate drips.

stages.name: tāla (cymbal)
stages.description: Sound 6; effect: drinks nectar.

stages.name: veṇu (flute)
stages.description: Sound 7; effect: secret knowledge.

stages.name: mṛdaṅga
stages.description: Sound 8; effect: the supreme speech.

stages.name: bherī
stages.description: Sound 9; effect: invisible body, divine eye.

stages.name: megha (thunder)
stages.description: Sound 10; effect: becomes Brahman.

name: Haṭhapradīpikā: the four stages of nāda

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: brahmagranthi pierced; bliss from the void; tinkling sounds; radiant, fragrant body

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: breath united enters the middle; viṣṇugranthi pierced; kettledrum sound in the extreme void

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: drum sound; breath in the great void, abode of powers; natural bliss

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: rudragranthi pierced; flute and vīṇā; mind one — rājayoga; liberation while living

notes: The HYP's form of the four stages (pth:hatha-four-stages, U51) keyed to the knots and the inner sounds. Banding is an interpretation: ārambha as one-pointed absorption in sound (B3), ghaṭa and paricaya as absorption with support (B4), niṣpatti = rājayoga = jīvanmukti (B7). The text has no separate 'seeing' stage (B5/B6); do not force one.

name: Haṭhapradīpikā: the order of practice

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: the first limb of haṭha: steadiness, health, lightness

stages.name: kumbhaka
stages.description: breath-control after purification of the channels

stages.name: mudrā / karaṇa
stages.description: the ten mudrās that awaken kuṇḍalinī

stages.name: nādānusandhāna
stages.description: the chief of the layas

stages.name: rājayoga (samādhi)
stages.description: the mindless state; liberation while living

notes: The sequence HYP 1.56 states (āsana, kumbhaka, mudrā, nādānusandhāna), practised 'until the fruit, rājayoga' (1.67). The yamas/niyamas (B1) are not a separate limb in the HYP. Banding by U28.

name: Prajāpati's four instructions to Indra (ChU 8.7-12)
description: Four successive teachings over 32 + 32 + 32 + 5 = 101 years, each tested by Indra until the last.

stages.name: the person seen in the eye / the reflected body
stages.description: Taught first; Virocana stops here and teaches the asuras that the body is the self; Indra sees the flaw.

stages.name: the one who moves about in dreams
stages.description: Not harmed by the body's defects, but seems to suffer.

stages.name: the one fully asleep, serene, seeing no dream
stages.description: Then one does not know oneself or beings, 'gone to annihilation as it were'.

stages.name: the serene one who reaches the highest light
stages.gloss: the bodiless self in its own form
stages.description: The body is the mortal base of the immortal bodiless self; rising from it, reaching the highest light, it appears in its own form.

notes: Stages 2-3 are provisional teachings, not practices; no band assigned. Advaita reads the sequence as superimposition and retraction (U13).

name: Kapila's sequence of devotion (Bhāgavata 3.25-29)

stages.name: sat-prasaṅga
stages.description: Attachment turned to the holy opens the door to liberation.

stages.name: kathā-śravaṇa
stages.description: In their company talks of the Lord's deeds arise, delightful to heart and ear.

stages.name: śraddhā, rati, bhakti
stages.description: Relishing them, faith, attraction and devotion follow in order.

stages.name: vairāgya and yoga
stages.gloss: dispassion and eight-limbed yoga with meditation on the Lord's form
stages.description: Devotion brings dispassion; the mind is held in yoga on the Lord.

stages.name: nirguṇa bhakti
stages.description: The mind flows to the Lord like the Gaṅgā to the sea.

stages.name: mad-bhāva
stages.description: Transcending the three guṇas, one attains the Lord; the mind reaches nirvāṇa and the body lives on while its karma lasts.

notes: Assembled by U06 from the Kapila Gītā's own ordering words (anukramiṣyati, 3.25.25); bands are interpretation-layer.

name: Kapila's yoga with a support (BhP 3.28)

stages.name: svadharma and restraints
stages.description: own dharma, contentment, service of knowers of self, non-harming, truth etc.

stages.name: āsana-jaya, prāṇa-jaya
stages.description: purifying the breath's path; breath burns faults

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: the senses drawn into the heart

stages.name: rūpa-dhyāna
stages.description: limb by limb, dwelling on glance and smile

stages.name: bhāva and release of the hook
stages.gloss: love, then letting go of the image
stages.description: melting love; the mind releases even its hook

stages.name: nirvāṇa of the mind
stages.gloss: the mind goes out like a flame
stages.description: free of support and object, the self seen as one without division

stages.name: siddha
stages.description: indifferent to the body, which lives on while karma lasts

notes: Within the Kapila Gītā (U06 owns the Gītā as a source); kept here because the coverage item names BhP 3.28.

name: The Kaṭha's inward withdrawal (KU 1.3.13)
description: A four-step withdrawal following the ladder of principles of KU 1.3.10-11, ending in the peaceful self.

stages.name: vāc → manas
stages.description: The wise one restrains speech in the mind.

stages.name: manas → jñāna ātman
stages.gloss: mind into the self that is knowledge
stages.description: Restrains that (mind) in the self that is knowledge (intellect).

stages.name: jñāna ātman → mahān ātmā
stages.description: Restrains knowledge in the great self.

stages.name: mahān → śānta ātman
stages.description: Restrains that in the peaceful self.

name: The seven modes of conduct (Kulārṇava)
notes: The Kulārṇava gives a ranking, not a description of inner stages; later tradition reads the seven as successive grades of eligibility. No bands assigned in Phase B (U51 to decide).

name: The seven ullāsas (Kulārṇava)

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: counted with the next four as 'waking'

stages.name: unmanā
stages.description: called 'dream'

stages.name: anavastha / samavasthā
stages.description: 'deep sleep', joined with the three states; knowing the seven one is liberated

notes: Stages of the Kula rite (restricted context). The text maps them onto waking, dream and deep sleep but gives no further content; bands left for U51.

name: The ascent through the centres (Kaulajñānanirṇaya 14)

stages.name: mūla-cakra
stages.description: Practice on the root centre: trembling, shaking, tongues, seals, frog-hopping (KJN 14.15–19).

stages.name: ādhāra and brahma-granthi
stages.description: Mind fixed four fingers above and at the brahma-knot; further signs and powers (KJN 14.20–37).

stages.name: hṛdaya
stages.description: Mind in the heart: samādhi with seizure and possession (KJN 14.38–43).

stages.name: kaṇṭha
stages.description: Mind at the throat-well: the scripture's truth arises in the mouth; deathlessness (KJN 14.44–49).

stages.name: lalāṭa and brahmarandhra
stages.description: Mind at the forehead and in the brahmarandhra: creator and destroyer; 'by mere knowing, through practice, one goes to liberation' (KJN 14.69–81).

stages.name: unmanī
stages.description: The mind void of void; the jīva dissolved, not roused by sound (KJN 14.82–88).

stages.name: dvādaśānta and amṛta
stages.description: The jewel-garland at the dvādaśānta; the nectar of Kaula nature; the supreme in which all dissolves; unstained by merit and sin (KJN 14.89–106).

notes: The chapter proceeds 'ataḥ ūrdhvam' (further upward) from centre to centre; ordering is the text's, stage names and bands are U21's.

name: Kumārila's way to release (Bhāṭṭa)

stages.name: kāmya-niṣiddha-varjana
stages.gloss: abstaining from desire-prompted and prohibited acts
stages.description: No new fruits requiring bodies are produced.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika-anuṣṭhāna
stages.description: To avoid the demerit of omission; Tantravārttika: also to destroy past sin.

stages.name: ātmajñāna
stages.description: Knowing the self (made firm by Vedānta); the self-knower no longer desires the fruits, so they do not accrue.

stages.name: bhoga (pūrvakriyākṣaya)
stages.description: Past karma is used up by experiencing its fruits.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: With no accumulation left no body arises; for Pārthasārathi, the absolute dissolution of the threefold bond, without bliss.

notes: The order is logical rather than strictly temporal (stages 1-4 run concurrently). Band B5 for self-knowledge is at most 'analogous': Kumārila does not treat it as a liberating insight.

name: The Goddess's ascent as kuṇḍalinī (Lalitā Sahasranāma 38-40)

stages.name: mūlādhāraika-nilayā
stages.description: The Goddess dwells solely in the mūlādhāra, asleep in the kula-pit.

stages.name: brahmagranthi-vibhedinī
stages.description: She pierces the first knot.

stages.name: maṇipūrāntar-uditā
stages.description: She rises in the navel centre.

stages.name: viṣṇugranthi-vibhedinī
stages.description: She pierces the second knot.

stages.name: ājñācakrāntarālasthā
stages.description: She abides in the centre between the brows.

stages.name: rudragranthi-vibhedinī
stages.description: She pierces the third knot.

stages.name: sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā
stages.description: She unites with her consort in the crown (SL 9).

stages.name: sudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī
stages.description: She showers nectar over the whole body and returns (SL 10).

notes: A description of the Goddess's movement in names; the texts do not give a method. Bands interpretive.

name: The Liṅga Purāṇa's eight means of yoga (LiP 1.8-9)

stages.name: yama
stages.description: non-harming first

stages.name: overcoming obstacles and upasargas
stages.gloss: renouncing the powers by supreme dispassion

name: Viśvanātha's elaboration of the stages from faith to love (Mādhuryakādambinī)

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: Faith arising from association with devotees and scripture.

stages.name: bhajana-kriyā (unsteady)
stages.description: Unsteady practice passes through six phases: utsāhamayī, ghana-taralā, vyūḍha-vikalpā, viṣaya-saṅgarā, niyamākṣamā, taraṅga-raṅgiṇī.

stages.name: anartha-nivṛtti
stages.description: Removal of the four kinds of anartha.

stages.name: niṣṭhā
stages.description: Freedom from sleepiness, distraction, incapacity, residual impurity and relish of other pleasures.

stages.name: ruci
stages.description: Taste for hearing, chanting and the rest for their own sake.

stages.name: āsakti
stages.description: Attachment to the Lord himself.

stages.name: bhāva
stages.description: The sprouting of love; visions and sphūrti of the Lord's play.

stages.name: prema
stages.description: Love, with direct experience of the Lord.

notes: Elaborates Rūpa's map (pth:rupa-gosvami-bhakti-stages, owned by U51). Chapter numbers approximate.

name: Mahā Upaniṣad: seven stages of ignorance and seven of knowledge

stages.name: bīja-jāgrat
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: jāgrat
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: mahā-jāgrat
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: jāgrat-svapna
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: svapna
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: svapna-jāgrat
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: suṣupti
stages.description: A stage of ignorance (no correspondence band).

stages.name: śubhecchā
stages.description: Wish for liberation: 'why do I remain a fool?'

stages.name: vicāraṇā
stages.description: Inquiry with the scriptures and the good.

stages.name: tanumānasī
stages.description: Mind made subtle by the first two.

stages.name: sattvāpatti
stages.description: Resting in the pure Self; the knower of Brahman.

stages.name: asaṃsakti
stages.description: Unattached; the excellent knower.

stages.name: padārthabhāvanā
stages.description: Objects no longer appear; woken only by others' effort.

stages.name: turyagā
stages.description: No difference; one's own nature.

name: Maharshi Mehi's graded practice

stages.name: mānas jap
stages.description: Mental repetition of the name.

stages.name: mānas dhyān
stages.description: Contemplating the guru's or deity's form.

stages.name: dṛṣṭi yoga
stages.description: Fixing the gaze at a point within, opening the inner light.

stages.name: nādānusandhān
stages.description: Following the inner sounds to the soundless.

stages.name: niḥśabda
stages.description: Beyond sound: realization of the Supreme.

name: From dharma to liberation (Rāmcaritmānas 3.16)

stages.name: dharma
stages.description: Keeping one's dharma.

stages.name: virati
stages.description: From dharma comes dispassion.

stages.name: yoga
stages.description: Yoga practised in dispassion.

stages.name: jñāna
stages.description: From yoga comes knowledge.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Knowledge gives liberation, as the Vedas say — but devotion, which melts the Lord at once, is set above this sequence.

name: The lamp of knowledge (Rāmcaritmānas 7.117–118)

stages.name: sāttvika śraddhā (the cow)
stages.description: Faith comes to dwell in the heart by Hari's grace.

stages.name: japa, tapa, vrata, yama-niyama (the grass)
stages.description: Faith is nourished by repetition, austerity, vows, restraints and Vedic good conduct.

stages.name: bhāva (the calf) and the milk of dharma
stages.description: Loving disposition draws forth the milk of highest dharma, milked by a pure mind into the vessel of trust.

stages.name: boiling, cooling and setting
stages.description: Boiled on desirelessness, cooled by contentment and forgiveness, set with fortitude and equanimity.

stages.name: churning by vicāra; the butter of vairāgya
stages.description: Churned by reflection with self-control and truthful speech, it yields pure dispassion.

stages.name: the fire of yoga; the ghee of jñāna
stages.description: Melted in yoga, burning good and bad karma, it becomes knowledge, 'mine-ness' burnt away.

stages.name: the lamp: citta, samatā, turīya wick
stages.description: Knowledge poured into the mind set on equanimity with the wick of the fourth state.

stages.name: so'ham asmi (the flame)
stages.description: The Self's experience shines and the delusion of difference, root of existence, is destroyed — unless māyā's powers and the senses blow the lamp out.

notes: The Mānas presents this path of knowledge in order to set above it devotion, the self-luminous gem that needs none of these stages and cannot be blown out (7.119–120).

name: Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa: eight limbs, tāraka and amanaska

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Conquering cold, heat, food and sleep; calm; sense-restraint.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Devotion to guru, contentment, solitude, dispassion.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: A comfortable seat.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Counts not reproduced.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Withdrawal of mind from objects.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Fixing the mind on consciousness.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: One-pointedness on the consciousness in all bodies.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Forgetting of meditation.

stages.name: tāraka
stages.description: Seeing the three targets and lights; śāmbhavī.

stages.name: amanaska
stages.description: Mind like an udder after milking; 'you are I'.

stages.name: paramahaṃsa avadhūta
stages.description: Mind dissolved in the supreme state of Viṣṇu; acts like a child or madman; sight purifies the world.

name: Dattātreya's yoga for Alarka (MkP 38-43)

stages.name: viveka
stages.gloss: discrimination of self and not-self; cutting 'mine'

stages.name: conduct and vows
stages.gloss: five vows, five observances, begging, the three staffs

stages.name: āsana and prāṇāyāma
stages.gloss: posture, breath, avoiding wrong places and times

stages.name: pratyāhāra and dhāraṇā
stages.gloss: withdrawal; ten bodily places of holding

stages.name: overcoming the upasargas
stages.gloss: turning from rewards and the five states

name: The Vedic course of dharma (Mīmāṃsā account)

stages.name: vedādhyayana
stages.gloss: study of one's Vedic recension from a teacher
stages.description: The student learns the Veda by the injunction of study.

stages.name: dharma-jijñāsā
stages.description: Before returning home the student inquires into the meaning of the Vedic sentences.

stages.name: agnyādhāna
stages.description: Becoming eligible (with one's wife) for the śrauta rites.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika karma
stages.description: Rites such as the Agnihotra and the new- and full-moon offerings, performed for life.

stages.name: kāmya karma
stages.description: Rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma for one desiring heaven; their fruit comes through the apūrva.

stages.name: svarga
stages.description: The fruit of the rites, understood as happiness; the self, not the burnt body, attains it.

notes: A reconstruction of the sequence implied by the texts, not a map the tradition itself numbers. Heaven receives no band because it is not liberation; the bands are interpretive (interpretation layer).

name: The limbs of yoga in the Mṛgendra (seven auxiliaries and yoga as the eighth)

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: exertion of breath by propelling, drawing in and holding; removes faults of ritual

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: turning the mind back from all objects once it tastes a little ease

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: the withdrawn mind fixed on a place chosen at will

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: thought directed again and again on that object

stages.name: vīkṣaṇa (ūha)
stages.description: scrutiny of the object: what is to be rejected and accepted, what sustains and opposes it

stages.name: japa
stages.description: uttering (its mantra), bringing the object of meditation face to face

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: when meditation becomes one continuous flow

stages.name: yoga (aṅgin)
stages.description: the eighth, the possessor of the limbs; powers shine forth like the sun's rays

notes: Order is the text's list order; the text says the limbs may be practised singly or together, so this is not strictly sequential. Bands are interpretive (U08); 'vīkṣaṇa' is banded B5 only tentatively (it is a discriminative scrutiny, not a stated seeing of the ultimate).

name: Muktikā: the path to liberation

stages.name: sādhana-catuṣṭaya
stages.description: Discrimination, dispassion, six virtues, longing for liberation.

stages.name: sadguru
stages.description: Approach with gifts; be tested.

stages.name: graded study
stages.description: Study as much as needed for knowledge to arise.

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: Hearing the Upaniṣads from the teacher.

stages.name: manana
stages.description: Reflecting on what is heard.

stages.name: nididhyāsana
stages.description: Contemplation, with destruction of vāsanā and dissolution of mind.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: Mind dissolved 'with form'; prārabdha continues.

stages.name: videhamukti
stages.description: At the body's fall, like pot-space or wind becoming still.

name: Nādabindu: the stages of the inner sound

stages.name: early sounds
stages.description: Like ocean, clouds, kettledrum, waterfall.

stages.name: middle sounds
stages.description: Like mardala drum, bell, horn.

stages.name: late sounds
stages.description: Like tinkling bells, flute, vīṇā, bee.

stages.name: mind absorbed in nāda
stages.description: Mind merges with nāda like milk with water.

stages.name: soundless / unmanī
stages.description: The soundless supreme Brahman; body like a log; liberated.

name: Who crosses māyā: the Nārada Bhakti Sūtra's sequence (NBS 46–50)

stages.name: saṅga-tyāga, mahānubhāva-sevā, nirmamatā
stages.gloss: giving up attachments, serving the great, freedom from 'mine'
stages.description: One who gives up attachments, serves the great souls and becomes free of 'mine'.

stages.name: vivikta-sthāna, loka-bandha-unmūlana, nistraiguṇya, yoga-kṣema-tyāga
stages.gloss: solitude, uprooting worldly bonds, going beyond the guṇas, giving up acquiring and keeping
stages.description: Resorting to a solitary place, uprooting the bonds of the world, going beyond the three guṇas, giving up the concern to acquire and keep.

stages.name: karma-phala-tyāga, karma-saṃnyāsa, nirdvandvatā
stages.gloss: giving up fruits, renouncing actions, then freedom from the pairs
stages.description: Giving up the fruit of actions, renouncing actions, and 'then' (tataḥ) becoming free of the pairs of opposites.

stages.name: veda-saṃnyāsa
stages.description: Renouncing even the Vedas (their ritual injunctions), laid down in the Lord.

stages.name: avicchinna-anurāga
stages.description: Obtaining unbroken, uninterrupted love.

stages.name: tarati
stages.description: He crosses (māyā), he crosses.

stages.name: lokāṃs tārayati
stages.description: He brings the worlds across.

notes: The sūtras list marks in groups; 'tataḥ' (then) in NBS 48 and the culmination in 49–50 suggest a sequence, which is how it is laid out here. Bands are interpretation-layer claims. The Nārada Sūtra also distinguishes secondary (gauṇī) from primary devotion (cpt:gauni-and-para-bhakti), not staged further.

name: The ascent of the liberated through the four forms (Nārāyaṇīya)

stages.name: freedom from merit and demerit
stages.description: Those free of fault, beyond merit and demerit, take the safe road (12.332.13).

stages.name: the sun as door
stages.description: The sun is the door; burnt by it, atom-like and invisible, they enter that god (12.332.13–14).

stages.name: Aniruddha
stages.description: Freed from the sun they abide in Aniruddha's body (12.332.15).

stages.name: Pradyumna
stages.description: Becoming mind, they enter Pradyumna (12.332.15).

stages.name: Saṃkarṣaṇa
stages.description: Freed from Pradyumna they enter the jīva Saṃkarṣaṇa — Sāṃkhyas together with Bhāgavatas (12.332.16).

stages.name: Vāsudeva
stages.description: Free of the three guṇas they enter the supreme self, the knower of the field, Vāsudeva, the dwelling of all; the one-pointed enter Vāsudeva directly (12.332.17–18; 12.336.3).

notes: A path of the liberated after death, not a sequence of practices; intermediate stages are left without bands. Janamejaya's question (12.336.3–4) calls the vyūha route the 'fourth path' and the ekāntins' direct entry the highest.

name: The stages of Nāth initiation

stages.name: approach and service
stages.description: Seeking a guru, being tested and serving (warned of the hardships).

stages.name: first initiation (aughaṛ)
stages.description: The guru cuts the top-knot, gives the mantra and the selī cord.

stages.name: probation
stages.description: A period of service and discipline under the guru.

stages.name: ear-splitting (darśanī / kānphaṭa)
stages.description: The ears are split and the earrings worn; a new name ending in -nāth and a panth.

notes: An institutional sequence rather than a map of realisation; stages as generally reported (to be sourced).

name: The Nyāya path to liberation (apavarga)

stages.name: jñānagrahaṇābhyāsa / śravaṇa
stages.gloss: study of the science of the self
stages.description: Study, retention, listening and reflection on the science of the self (NS 4.2.47; NBh).

stages.name: ātmasaṃskāra: yama and niyama
stages.description: Restraints common to all life-stages and particular observances remove demerit and increase merit (NS 4.2.46; NBh).

stages.name: saṃvāda / manana
stages.description: Discussion with the learned and reasoned examination through the sixteen categories, to cut doubt and confirm what is ascertained (NS 4.2.47–49; NK 1.3).

stages.name: yoga and adhyātmavidhi
stages.gloss: yoga in solitude; the method of the inner self
stages.description: Yoga in forests, caves and sandbanks; austerity, breath-control, sense-withdrawal, meditation, fixation; contemplation of objects and of the body (prasaṅkhyāna) (NS 4.2.42, 4.2.46; NBh 4.2.2, 4.2.46).

stages.name: samādhiviśeṣābhyāsa
stages.description: Repeated practice of a special samādhi, from which knowledge of truth arises (NS 4.2.38).

stages.name: tattvajñāna
stages.description: Knowledge of the self and the other objects of knowledge as they are; the I-notion ceases (NS 1.1.1, 4.2.1; NBh 1.1.1).

stages.name: removal of false knowledge, faults and activity
stages.gloss: the chain undone; the detached dweller
stages.description: False knowledge removed, faults, activity and further birth fall away (NS 1.1.2); for one whose afflictions have waned, activity does not lead to rebirth (NS 4.1.64); one who dwells detached within and without is called liberated (NBh 4.2.2).

stages.name: apavarga
stages.description: With birth ended, pain ends absolutely: liberation (NS 1.1.22).

notes: The order is a reconstruction from separate sūtras (the texts do not number stages). Bands are interpretive; stage 7 is given B8 because the Bhāṣya calls the detached dweller 'liberated' while embodied, before final release (B7).

name: The seven states of the jīva (Pañcadaśī 7)

stages.name: ajñāna
stages.description: not knowing the self (the ten men not counting themselves)

stages.name: āvaraṇa
stages.description: 'the tenth is not there, it does not shine'

stages.name: vikṣepa
stages.description: grief, wrong notions ('the tenth is lost')

stages.name: parokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'there is a tenth' — knowledge from the teacher's word not yet one's own

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'you are the tenth' — recognizing oneself as Brahman

stages.name: śoka-nivṛtti
stages.description: grief ends with recognition

stages.name: niraṅkuśa-tṛpti
stages.description: the satisfaction of one who has done all that is to be done (jīvanmukti)

notes: Illustrated by the tenth-man story. Bands are interpretive.

name: Learning, childlikeness, silence (BAU 3.5.1)
description: The stages of the knower who has renounced, as stated to Kahola.

stages.name: vyutthāna
stages.description: Knowing the self, brahmins rise above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds and live as mendicants.

stages.name: pāṇḍitya
stages.description: Having done with learning ...

stages.name: bālya
stages.description: ... he should live as a child.

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: Having done with childhood and learning, he becomes a silent sage.

stages.name: brāhmaṇa
stages.description: Having done with silence and non-silence, he becomes a brahmin.

notes: The meaning of bālya (childlike state; Śaṅkara relates it to the strength of knowledge) is not settled; no band.

name: The nine steps to the supreme abode (Paramapadasopānam)

stages.name: viveka
stages.description: Discerning self from body and the Lord as master.

stages.name: nirveda
stages.description: Grief at one's past and at worldly life.

stages.name: virakti
stages.description: Turning away from lesser ends.

stages.name: bhīti
stages.description: Fear of continued rebirth.

stages.name: prasādana (prasāda-hetu)
stages.description: Surrender, which wins the Lord's grace.

stages.name: utkramaṇa
stages.description: Leaving the body through the head channel.

stages.name: arcirādi
stages.description: Travelling by the path of light.

stages.name: divyadeśa-prāpti
stages.description: Arrival in Vaikuṇṭha across the Virajā.

stages.name: prāpti
stages.description: Attaining the Lord and eternal service.

notes: Names of the nine steps recalled with low confidence; check the text.

name: The five stages of the Pāśupata path (avasthā-pañcaka)

stages.name: vyakta (manifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which the Pāśupata sign is shown
stages.description: After initiation the brahmin lives in the temple under his teacher, bathes and lies in ash, wears the used garland, worships with laughter, song, dance, the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostration and muttering, keeps the ten restraints and lives on alms. Place: the teacher. Gain: knowledge. Purification: removal of turbidity.
stages.ref: GK 5-7; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 2, 5, 6; PS 1.2-1.17; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: avyakta (unmanifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which sign and learning are hidden
stages.description: With the teacher's leave, having gained knowledge, he goes among people with his sign hidden and courts dishonour by feigned sleep, trembling, limping, amorous gestures, senseless acts and speech, and by wandering like a madman on discarded food; revilers take his demerit and give him their merit. Place: people. Gain: austerity (the whole of dharma).
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 3.1-4.18; PABh on PS 3.12-17, 5.29

stages.name: jaya (conquest)
stages.gloss: the stage of conquering the senses
stages.description: In an empty house or cave he conquers the senses, recites the chosen Gāyatrī, meditates on Oṃ with fixation in the heart and remains constantly with the god; after six months of constant yoga the powers arise in abundance. Place: cave. Gain: constant union with the god.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 5.1-25; PABh on PS 5.13, 5.29

stages.name: cheda (cutting)
stages.gloss: the stage ending in the cutting [of bonds]
stages.description: He lives in the cremation ground until the body falls, on whatever comes, always remembering Rudra; he attains union with Rudra. Place: cremation ground. Gain: steadiness / union.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5, 6; PS 5.30-34; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: niṣṭhā (completion)
stages.gloss: the stage in which all activity has ceased
stages.description: All the practitioner's activity has ceased; without body, his place is Rudra alone; having cut the root of the faults and fixed the mind on Rudra, vigilant, he reaches the end of sufferings by the Lord's grace and does not return. Gain: perfection (the Lord's qualities).

notes: Stage names from the Gaṇakārikā; Kauṇḍinya gives the same progression through residence, livelihood, strength, action, purification and gain. Initiation (B0) precedes stage 1. Bands are interpretation-layer claims: the first two stages are ascetic-ritual preparation (B2), conquest of the senses in solitude is withdrawal and concentration (B3, with absorption and powers as it matures), the cremation-ground stage is deepening after the powers (B6), completion is final liberation (B7). The Ratnaṭīkā rejects a separate 'stage of the perfected'.

name: The Prābhākara way to release (Śālikanātha)

stages.name: saṃsāra-udvega
stages.gloss: aversion to the sorrows of saṃsāra
stages.description: Troubled by worldly sorrows and indifferent even to the pleasures mixed with them, one rises for release.

stages.name: niṣiddha-kāmya-nivṛtti
stages.gloss: turning from prohibited and desire-prompted acts
stages.description: Abstaining from the causes of bondage and from means to prosperity.

stages.name: bhoga
stages.description: Dharma and adharma already produced are exhausted by being experienced.

stages.name: ātmajñāna with śama, dama, brahmacarya
stages.gloss: self-knowledge supported by calm, restraint, celibacy
stages.description: Enjoined for non-return, it destroys the remaining store of karma.

stages.name: dehoccheda
stages.description: The self remains in mere being, all-pervading, without cognition or bliss.

notes: Sequence as stated in one passage; bands are interpretive.

name: Bhoja's ladder of samprajñāta samādhi (RM 1.17–18)

stages.name: savitarka
stages.description: Cultivation on gross elements and senses, mixed with word and meaning; grasped-coalescence.

stages.name: nirvitarka
stages.description: The same object without sequence and word.

stages.name: savicāra
stages.description: On subtle objects (tanmātras, inner organ) delimited by place, time, property.

stages.name: nirvicāra
stages.description: The subtle object as property-bearer alone.

stages.name: sānanda
stages.description: Cultivating the inner organ's sattva tinged by rajas and tamas; grasping-coalescence; those who stop here are 'videhas'.

stages.name: sāsmita
stages.description: Cultivating pure sattva, mere being; those who stop here are 'prakṛtilayas'.

stages.name: viveka-khyāti (grahītṛ-samāpatti)
stages.description: For those who know the supreme puruṣa and continue cultivation.

stages.name: asamprajñāta
stages.description: Rejecting every arising activity 'not this, not this'; only impressions remain.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log).

name: The Rāma Gītā's path from duty to merging (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 7.5)

stages.name: sva-varṇāśrama-kriyā
stages.gloss: duties of one's class and stage
stages.description: Performing prescribed actions purifies the mind.

stages.name: sad-guru-āśraya
stages.description: Giving up the means already used, one approaches a teacher for self-knowledge.

stages.name: karma-tyāga, ātmānusandhāna
stages.description: Since knowledge and action cannot be combined, the seeker gives up action and inquires.

stages.name: vākyārtha-jñāna
stages.gloss: knowing the meaning of 'that thou art'
stages.description: By faith, the teacher's grace and partial implication the identity is known.

stages.name: samādhi / praṇava-laya
stages.gloss: meditation dissolving A-U-M into the Self
stages.description: Contemplating 'I am light, unborn...' and dissolving the syllables of Oṃ.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: Free of bonds, the sage lives out his remaining karma.

stages.name: mayi pravilaya
stages.description: He merges in Rāma like water in water, space in space.

notes: Assembled by U06 from the order stated in the Rāma Gītā; the text adds that until all is seen as Rāma one should worship him (7.5.58). Bands are interpretation-layer (B8 before B7 reflects the text's order: jīvanmukti, then final merging).

name: The ladder of goals in Caitanya's dialogue with Rāmānanda Rāya (CC 2.8)

stages.name: varṇāśrama-dharma
stages.description: Worship of Viṣṇu through one's social duties — called 'external'.

stages.name: karmārpaṇa
stages.description: Offering the fruits of all action to Kṛṣṇa — 'external'.

stages.name: svadharma-tyāga
stages.description: Abandoning social duty for refuge in Kṛṣṇa — 'external'.

stages.name: jñāna-miśrā bhakti
stages.description: Devotion still aimed at knowledge — 'external'.

stages.name: jñāna-śūnyā bhakti
stages.description: Giving up the effort for knowledge and living by hearing (BhP 10.14.3) — 'this is so; go further'.

stages.name: prema-bhakti
stages.description: Love of God as the essence of all goals.

stages.name: kānta-prema
stages.description: The love of the gopīs, highest among the relationships.

stages.name: rādhā-prema
stages.description: Rādhā's love as the crown of all.

stages.name: prema-vilāsa-vivarta
stages.description: The state where lover and beloved lose the sense of separateness, expressed in Rāmānanda's song; Caitanya closes Rāmānanda's mouth.

notes: Order and wording as recalled from CC 2.8 (c. vv. 57–195); the ladder is a dialogue, not a practice sequence; B-bands are interpretive.

name: The ladder of births to name-recitation (Rudrayāmala, quoted by Bhāskararāya)

stages.name: dīkṣita
stages.gloss: initiated after many births of merit
stages.description: Only after many births of merit is one initiated.

stages.name: śiva-viṣṇu-parāyaṇa
stages.description: By great fortune one becomes devoted to Śiva or Viṣṇu.

stages.name: śakti-bhāva
stages.description: Then the disposition toward Śakti arises.

stages.name: sundarī-bhāva
stages.description: Then by great good fortune the disposition toward Sundarī (Tripurasundarī).

stages.name: turīyā antargatā
stages.description: Then the fourth is reached within.

stages.name: nāma-saṅkīrtana
stages.description: Rarest of all, the singing of her names.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: In that birth the Goddess, pleased, grants liberation while living; nothing more remains to be done.

notes: Known here through Bhāskararāya's quotation of the Rudrayāmala (checked in the local e-text).

name: The three stages of the Sahajiyā path

stages.name: pravarta
stages.description: Reliance on the name (nāma) and the guru's mantra; ordinary Vaiṣṇava practice.

stages.name: sādhaka
stages.description: Reliance on bhāva; the esoteric discipline with the partner begins (restricted; not described).

stages.name: siddha
stages.description: Resting in prema; the sahaja state of the innate Man.

notes: Scheme (pravarta–sādhaka–siddha, with the āśrayas of nāma, bhāva, prema) widely reported for Sahajiyā manuals; some sources add a preliminary 'sthūla' stage (low confidence).

name: The ten acts (daśakārya / tacakāriyam) of Tamil Śaiva Siddhānta

stages.name: tattva-rūpa
stages.gloss: seeing the form of the tattvas
stages.description: discerning the 36 tattvas that make body and world

stages.name: tattva-darśana
stages.description: seeing them as not-self and inert

stages.name: tattva-śuddhi
stages.description: ceasing to identify with them

stages.name: ātma-rūpa
stages.description: knowing the soul as knower dependent on grace

stages.name: ātma-darśana
stages.description: seeing that the soul knows only through Śiva

stages.name: ātma-śuddhi
stages.description: giving up the sense of independent agency

stages.name: śiva-rūpa
stages.description: knowing Śiva as grace working in the soul

stages.name: śiva-darśana
stages.description: seeing Śiva with the eye of grace

stages.name: śiva-yoga
stages.description: inseparable union, the soul's acts being Śiva's

stages.name: śiva-bhoga
stages.description: abiding in Śiva's bliss

notes: Bands are U18's interpretive proposal (interpretation layer).

name: The Sāṃkhya Kārikā's path from suffering to isolation

stages.name: jijñāsā
stages.description: Struck by the three sufferings and finding seen remedies uncertain and impermanent, one seeks their destroyer.

stages.name: turning from Vedic means
stages.description: Vedic means are impure, perishable and graded; discriminating knowledge is better.

stages.name: approaching the teacher; study, hearing, reasoning
stages.description: Study, hearing, reasoning, a knowing friend and service to the venerable bring knowledge of the principles; error, incapacity and contentment are abandoned.

stages.name: tattvābhyāsa
stages.description: Long, reverent, uninterrupted contemplation of the principles.

stages.name: nāsmi na me nāham
stages.gloss: 'I am not, not mine, not I'
stages.description: The complete, pure, single discriminating knowledge arises.

stages.name: prakṛti ceases for the seer
stages.description: Puruṣa sees prakṛti, her purpose served, withdrawn like a dancer; no motive for further creation remains.

stages.name: dhṛtaśarīra
stages.description: Virtue and the rest no longer cause; the knower remains embodied by the momentum of impressions, like a potter's wheel.

stages.name: kaivalya
stages.description: At the body's end, pradhāna having ceased, final isolation.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments (see interpretation_log).

name: The Sāṃkhya Sūtra's path of meditation and discrimination

stages.name: hearing instruction repeatedly
stages.description: Instruction in the truth (like the king's son), repeated, with reflection; mere hearing is not enough because latent tendencies are strong.

stages.name: one's own duty, posture, concentration, breath
stages.description: Performing the duties of one's stage of life, steady and pleasant posture, concentration, restraint by expulsion and retention; dispassion and practice.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Cessation of mental modifications; mind without object; turning from torpor and distraction.

stages.name: tattvābhyāsa by 'neti neti'
stages.description: Giving up each principle with 'not this, not this'.

stages.name: vivekasiddhi
stages.description: Discrimination of puruṣa and prakṛti; liberation comes from knowledge alone.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: Experience continues by residual impressions, like a whirling wheel; the liberated living teach.

stages.name: kṛtakṛtyatā
stages.description: Complete cessation of suffering through discrimination.

notes: Stages ordered from the sūtras' own sequence; bands are interpretive.

name: The life-cycle of sacraments (saṃskāra), conception to ancestorhood

stages.name: vedārambha / vedavratas
stages.gloss: beginning of Vedic study and the Veda-vows

notes: A life-cycle of rites rather than a soteriological path; bands are given only where a stage corresponds to entry, discipline or ethical foundation. Lists vary between texts.

name: Śāṇḍilya: the eight-limbed yoga

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Ten restraints.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Ten observances.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Named postures.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Breath-regulation (counts not reproduced).

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Five kinds of withdrawal.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Concentration.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation with or without qualities.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Union of jīvātman and paramātman, free of the triad.

name: The sequence of the renunciation rite

stages.name: vairāgya and eligibility
stages.description: Renounce the day dispassion arises; eligibility examined; consent of kin.

stages.name: kṛcchra
stages.description: Expiatory penances.

stages.name: aṣṭa-śrāddha
stages.description: To gods, seers, divine beings, humans, elements, fathers, mothers and oneself — a ritual death.

stages.name: virajā-homa
stages.description: Oblations that purify the elements of the body.

stages.name: agni-samāropa
stages.description: The sacred fires taken into oneself; Sāvitrī into the vyāhṛtis.

stages.name: praiṣa
stages.description: 'I have risen above the desires for wife, wealth and worlds'; 'I have renounced' thrice.

stages.name: abhaya
stages.description: 'Fearlessness to all beings from me'.

stages.name: liṅga-tyāga / liṅga-grahaṇa
stages.description: Topknot and thread abandoned into water; staff, cloth, water-pot taken (or kept for life in the Vaiṣṇava rite).

stages.name: upadeśa
stages.description: The guru gives praṇava and the great saying.

name: The grades of renouncer

stages.name: kuṭīcaka
stages.description: Keeps topknot, thread, staff; eats in one place; external worship; reaches the earthly worlds.

stages.name: bahūdaka
stages.description: Triple staff; eight mouthfuls from many houses; reaches heaven.

stages.name: haṃsa
stages.description: Matted hair; alms unplanned; mental worship; reaches the world of austerity.

stages.name: paramahaṃsa
stages.description: No topknot or thread; hand as bowl; reaches the world of truth; for him no dharma or adharma.

stages.name: turīyātīta
stages.description: Takes food like a cow; naked; body as corpse; kaivalya in the Self.

stages.name: avadhūta
stages.description: No rule; python's way; beyond castes and stages; acts as child, madman or ghost.

name: The order of the aṅgas in the Rajasthani Sant anthologies

stages.name: gurudev
stages.description: Meeting and honouring the true guru.

stages.name: sumiran
stages.description: Remembrance of the Name.

stages.name: birah
stages.description: The burning of separation.

stages.name: gyān-birah
stages.description: Separation turned to knowledge (Kabīr Granthāvalī).

stages.name: paracā
stages.description: Direct encounter with the Lord: light, unstruck sound, nectar.

stages.name: ras / jarṇā / hairān
stages.description: Tasting the Lord, bearing it quietly, wonder.

stages.name: lai
stages.description: Absorption (laya) in the Lord.

notes: CAUTION: this is the editorial order of topics in the Dādūpanthī anthologies (Kabīr Granthāvalī, Dādū Vāṇī), not a ladder the texts themselves declare; recorded because the order recurs and reads as a progression. Aṅga names moderate-to-low confidence.

name: The ascent through the inner regions (Sant Mat)

stages.name: nām-dān and the vows
stages.description: Initiation by a living master; vegetarian diet, abstinence, moral life, daily meditation.

stages.name: tīsrā til (eye centre)
stages.description: Simran and dhyān gather the attention at the eye centre; the body is left behind as at death.

stages.name: Sahasdal Kanwal
stages.description: First region; bell and conch; the flame of Jot Nirañjan; the astral region.

stages.name: Trikuṭī
stages.description: Region of Brahm and the universal mind; drum/thunder; the causal region, still within Kāl's domain.

stages.name: Daswān Dwār / Sunn
stages.description: The soul, free of the three bodies and the mind, sees itself as spirit ('self-realization'); sārangī.

stages.name: Mahāsunn
stages.description: A region of darkness crossed only with the master's help.

stages.name: Bhanwar Guphā
stages.description: Flute.

stages.name: Sach Khand / Sat Lok
stages.description: The soul meets the Sat Purush ('God-realization'); vīṇā; beyond the reach of birth and death.

stages.name: Alakh Lok and Agam Lok
stages.description: Higher purely spiritual regions.

stages.name: Anāmī / Radhasoami Dhām
stages.description: The supreme, the ocean from which the soul came.

notes: Beas-line version. Sant Mat itself holds that the absorption of other yogas ends at Sahasdal Kanwal or Trikuṭī (B4 here); it would reject any alignment of those regions with liberation.
