stages.description: After the channels are purified: lightness, radiance, strong digestion, a fragrant and beautiful body; in breath-control sweat (to be rubbed in), trembling, frog-like hopping and rising from the ground; the danger of women's attraction and loss of bindu; repetition of the praṇava against obstacles.

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: Prāṇa and apāna, nāda and bindu, the individual and supreme self join; the retention is lengthened and the senses are withdrawn, whatever is perceived being regarded as the self; powers arise that are to be hidden.

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: The breath, with the fire, awakens kuṇḍalinī and enters the suṣumnā; the centres are pierced; the yogin sees the 'three peaks' of his karma and destroys them; the five element-concentrations are practised.

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: Samādhi by one's own act; crossing the seeds of beginningless karma one drinks the nectar; the yogin is liberated while living and may leave the body at will or roam the worlds with the powers.

notes: Complements U28's pth:hyp-nada-four-stages (the same four names read through the inner sounds) and U51's pth:hatha-four-stages. Bands are interpretive.

name: The Vedic ritual career: from initiation to the soma rites and the world of the fathers

stages.name: upanayana
stages.description: The teacher takes the student in as an embryo and imparts the Sāvitrī (AVŚ 11.5.3; RV 3.62.10).

stages.name: brahmacarya and svādhyāya
stages.description: Life with the teacher in fuel, girdle, toil and tapas; learning one's śākhā by recitation (AVŚ 11.5; RV 7.103.5).

stages.name: agnyādhāna
stages.gloss: establishing the fires (as a married householder)
stages.description: The householder and his wife establish the three fires.

stages.name: agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa
stages.description: Lifelong daily and new/full-moon offerings.

stages.name: cāturmāsya, paśubandha
stages.description: Seasonal rites (incl. the Tryambaka offerings) and the animal sacrifice.

stages.name: dīkṣā and agniṣṭoma
stages.gloss: consecration and the first soma sacrifice
stages.description: 'Here I go from untruth to truth'; the soma pressed, offered and drunk: 'we have become immortal' (VS 1.5; RV 8.48.3).

stages.name: further soma rites; agnicayana; (for kings) rājasūya, aśvamedha
stages.description: Greater soma rites and the fire altar, opened by the yoking of the mind (VS 11.1–5).

stages.name: pitṛmedha: to Yama and the fathers
stages.description: At death, carried by Agni to the fathers and Yama in the highest heaven, rejoined with iṣṭāpūrta (RV 10.14.8); the ideal before it, a full life of a hundred autumns.

notes: The Saṃhitās do not present a staged liberation path; this is the ritual sequence the śrauta lineages follow (its order is fixed in the sūtras, U02). Bands are interpretive: the final stage is left unbanded because heaven (svarga) is not liberation in the band scale's sense, and the later tradition itself distinguishes them.

name: The nine enclosures of the Śrīcakra as a sequence

stages.name: trailokyamohana-cakra (bhūpura)
stages.description: Presiding goddess Tripurā; Prakaṭa yoginīs; the powers Aṇimā etc., the eight Mothers (in the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad the six passions with merit and demerit), the ten mudrā-powers.

stages.name: sarvāśāparipūraka-cakra (16 petals)
stages.description: Tripureśī; Gupta yoginīs; the sixteen attractions (in the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad the elements, senses and mind).

stages.name: sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra (8 petals)
stages.description: Tripurasundarī; Guptatara yoginīs; the eight Anaṅga goddesses (speech, grasping, going, excreting, bliss, rejecting, accepting, indifference).

stages.name: sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka-cakra (14 triangles)
stages.description: Tripuravāsinī; Sampradāya yoginīs; the fourteen channels.

stages.name: sarvārthasādhaka-cakra (outer 10)
stages.description: Tripurāśrī; Kulottīrṇa yoginīs; the ten vital airs.

stages.name: sarvarakṣākara-cakra (inner 10)
stages.description: Tripuramālinī; Nigarbha yoginīs; the ten fires.

stages.name: sarvarogahara-cakra (8 triangles)
stages.description: Tripurāsiddhā; Rahasya yoginīs; the eight goddesses of speech.

stages.name: sarvasiddhiprada-cakra (triangle)
stages.description: Tripurāmbā; Atirahasya yoginīs; Kāmeśvarī, Vajreśvarī, Bhagamālinī (the unmanifest, mahat, ahaṃkāra).

stages.name: sarvānandamaya-cakra (bindu)
stages.description: Mahātripurasundarī with Kāmeśvara; Parāparātirahasya yoginī; the non-difference of knower, knowing and known.

notes: The texts present the enclosures as the order of worship (from outer to inner); the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad maps them onto body and mind and makes the centre the non-duality of knower and known. Reading the order as stages of attainment, and the bands, are interpretive (low confidence). Names of the cakras and yoginī classes from memory.

name: The way of surrender (Śrīvaiṣṇava prapatti)

stages.name: ācārya-samāśrayaṇa
stages.description: Seeking out a true teacher of the lineage.

stages.name: pañcasaṃskāra
stages.description: Initiation with the marks, name, mantras and instruction in worship.

stages.name: artha-pañcaka and rahasya-traya
stages.gloss: learning the five things and the three secrets
stages.description: Learning the nature of self, Lord, means, goal and obstacle, and the meaning of the three mantras.

stages.name: ākiñcanya and ananyagatitva
stages.description: Knowing oneself to have no means and no other refuge.

stages.name: prapatti
stages.description: Taking refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī — performed as a means (Vaṭakalai) or accepted as the Lord's being the means (Teṅkalai); after it one has done what is to be done.

stages.name: uttarakṛtya: life of service
stages.description: Service to the Lord and his devotees, recollection of the dvaya, avoidance of offences, duties as command (V) or as service (T).

stages.name: niryāṇa and arcirādi
stages.gloss: departure and the path of light
stages.description: At the end of the body the Lord himself leads the soul out and along the path of light; no last remembrance needed.

stages.name: paripūrṇa-brahmānubhava
stages.description: In Vaikuṇṭha the soul's nature is manifest and it enjoys the Lord fully.

stages.name: nitya-kainkarya
stages.description: Eternal service to the divine couple.

notes: Assembled from Deśika's and Piḷḷai Lokācārya's works; the two schools differ on stage 5 (means or acceptance) and 6 (duties as command or as service). Band B5 for surrender is interpretive: the tradition treats it as the decisive, irreversible act after which liberation is certain.

name: The Śrīvidyā sequence of initiation and worship (Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra)

stages.name: dīkṣā and Bālā
stages.description: Initiation (śāktī, śāmbhavī, māntrī); the guru's pādukā; the Bālā mantra, then the chosen mantra; an initiatory name ending in '-ānandanātha'.

stages.name: gaṇanāyaka-paddhati
stages.description: Removal of obstacles to the worship of the great vidyā.

stages.name: śrīkrama
stages.description: Purifications, the seat, placements (nyāsa), the special water and the visualization of the Goddess's world in the cakra.

stages.name: lalitā-krama
stages.description: Invocation of the Goddess into the bindu, the sixty-four services, the fifteen Nityās.

stages.name: lalitā-navāvaraṇa-pūjā
stages.description: The full worship of the Śrīcakra enclosure by enclosure.

stages.name: śyāmā-krama and vārāhī-krama
stages.description: Worship of Śyāmā (Mantriṇī) and Vārāhī (Daṇḍinī).

stages.name: parā-krama
stages.description: Worship of the supreme Goddess Parā.

stages.name: homa and the common rules
stages.description: Fire rite and the rules common to all worship.

stages.name: kṛtakṛtyatā / jīvanmukti
stages.description: One steadfast in kula who knows and performs all this has accomplished everything; wherever he dies he is liberated while living.

notes: Stages follow the order of the Kalpasūtra's ten sections. Later manuals add further consecrations (e.g. the sixteen-syllable vidyā and pūrṇābhiṣeka) — not recorded here as stages because their sequence was not checked. Bands are interpretive.

name: Tejobindu: the fifteen limbs

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Sense-restraint by knowledge 'all is Brahman'.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Flow of like thoughts.

stages.name: tyāga
stages.description: Abandoning the world-appearance.

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: Silence where words return.

stages.name: deśa
stages.gloss: the solitary place — where all is pervaded
stages.description: The solitary place — where all is pervaded.

stages.name: kāla
stages.description: Time — the partless.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: The seat where Brahman-contemplation flows.

stages.name: mūlabandha
stages.description: Brahman, root of worlds.

stages.name: dehasāmya
stages.description: Dissolving in the even Brahman.

stages.name: dṛksthiti
stages.description: Seeing the world as Brahman.

stages.name: prāṇasaṃyamana
stages.gloss: stopping modifications by seeing all as Brahman
stages.description: Stopping modifications by seeing all as Brahman.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Seeing the Self in objects.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.gloss: holding the mind wherever it goes in Brahman
stages.description: Holding the mind wherever it goes in Brahman.

stages.name: ātmadhyāna
stages.description: 'I am Brahman alone'.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Forgetting of the modification.

name: The three dispositions (paśu, vīra, divya)

stages.name: paśubhāva
stages.description: purity, restraint, solitude, freedom from desire and anger, breath-yoga, reliance on the Vedic path (Rudrayāmala 17.136-140); 'always pure' (Kālīvilāsa 6.10)

stages.name: vīrabhāva
stages.description: the fearless adept of the Kaula rite and cremation ground (restricted)

stages.name: divyabhāva
stages.description: seeing all as divine; proper to the first ages in the Kālīvilāsa

notes: Whether the three are successive stages of one practitioner or fixed temperaments/ages is itself treated differently by the texts (dsp:bhavas-in-kali-yuga). Only the first stage is banded (on the Rudrayāmala's description).

name: Tirumūlar's eight limbs (aṭṭāṅka yōkam, TM 3rd tantra)

stages.name: iyamam
stages.description: Non-killing, truth, non-stealing, continence and the other restraints.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: niyamam
stages.description: Purity, austerity, study (including hearing the Siddhānta), worship of Śiva.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: ātaṉam
stages.description: The countless postures, of which the text praises a few as chief.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: pirāṇāyāmam
stages.description: Fitting control of the breath (summary; see prc:vasi-yoga).
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: pirattiyākāram
stages.description: Withdrawing the senses from their objects.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: tāraṇai
stages.description: Holding the mind firm.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: tiyāṉam
stages.description: Meditation.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

stages.name: camāti
stages.description: Samādhi; the text follows it with the fruits of the eight limbs and the eight great powers.
stages.ref: TM 552 and sections 2–9 of the 3rd tantra

notes: The third tantra's sections (checked in the local e-text) run: aṭṭāṅka yōkam, iyamam, niyamam, ātaṉam, pirāṇāyāmam, pirattiyākāram, tāraṇai, tiyāṉam, camāti, aṭṭāṅkayōkap pēṟu, aṭṭamā citti, … kāyacitti upāyam, kāla cakkaram, āyuḷ parīṭcai, vāra caram, vāra cūlam, kēcari, pariyaṅka, amuri tāraṇai, cantira yōkam. Stage descriptions are brief summaries at moderate confidence. Shared with lin:nayanmar (U18).

name: The order of approach in the Tiruppāvai (as read by the Śrīvaiṣṇava commentators)

stages.name: the vow resolved
stages.gloss: Nārāyaṇa himself will give us the drum
stages.description: The call to the Mārkaḻi vow and the certainty that the Lord alone gives the goal.

stages.name: the observances
stages.gloss: what we do and do not do
stages.description: Singing his feet, restraint in food and adornment, no forbidden acts, no evil words, alms.

stages.name: pure worship
stages.description: Coming pure, strewing flowers, singing with the mouth and meditating with the mind; faults burn like cotton.

stages.name: waking the companions
stages.description: Going from house to house to wake the other girls — the devotees are sought first.

stages.name: the gatekeepers and the elders
stages.gloss: approach through those who guard the Lord's house
stages.description: Waking the gatekeeper, Nandagopa, Yaśodā and Balarāma.

stages.name: Nappiṉṉai the mediator
stages.description: Waking Nappiṉṉai and asking her to open the door and bring them to Kṛṣṇa.

stages.name: before the Lord
stages.gloss: praise and petition in his presence
stages.description: Waking Kṛṣṇa, praising his deeds, asking him to rise to his throne and hear them.

stages.name: nothing of our own; the unbreakable relation
stages.gloss: ākiñcanya and the plea of kinship
stages.description: 'We are ignorant cowherds; our relation with you cannot be broken; forgive our small names for you.'

stages.name: service forever
stages.gloss: the true meaning of the drum
stages.description: 'Not the drum today: kinship and service to you alone for seven times seven births; change our other desires.'

stages.name: the fruit for those who recite
stages.description: Those who recite the thirty receive the Lord's grace everywhere.

notes: The reading of the verse-sequence as an order of approach (devotees → ācārya-like gatekeepers → Śrī as mediator → the Lord → service) is the Śrīvaiṣṇava commentators' as recalled; verse ranges and the gatekeeper = teacher reading low-to-moderate confidence. Bands are interpretation-layer claims and fit a devotional approach map only loosely.

name: Triśikhibrāhmaṇa: the limbs of the yoga of knowledge

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Dispassion toward body and senses.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Constant attachment to the supreme.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Indifference to all things.

stages.name: prāṇasaṃyama
stages.description: Knowing the world as unreal.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The mind turned inward.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Motionless mind.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: 'I am pure consciousness'.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Forgetting of meditation; 'I am the supreme Brahman'.

name: Action, then knowledge or devotion (Uddhava Gītā 11.20)

stages.name: karma-yoga
stages.gloss: action without desire, offered to the Lord
stages.description: One performs action until disgust (nirveda) or faith (śraddhā) arises.

stages.name: jñāna-yoga (for the nirviṇṇa)
stages.description: For the one disgusted with action who has renounced it.

stages.name: bhakti-yoga (for the śraddhāvān)
stages.description: For one in whom faith in the Lord's stories has arisen, neither disgusted nor over-attached.

stages.name: siddhi
stages.description: Purified, one attains knowledge or devotion; the human body is the boat, the teacher the helmsman.

notes: Branching map: stage 2 has two alternatives by disposition.

name: The stages of love from prema to mahābhāva (Ujjvalanīlamaṇi)

stages.name: prema
stages.description: Love that never breaks despite causes for breaking.

stages.name: sneha
stages.description: Love that melts the heart and illumines it.

stages.name: māna
stages.description: Love that conceals itself in crookedness.

stages.name: praṇaya
stages.description: Love free of reverence, feeling oneness.

stages.name: rāga
stages.description: Sorrow becomes happiness for the beloved.

stages.name: anurāga
stages.description: The beloved ever fresh.

stages.name: bhāva / mahābhāva
stages.description: Found only in the gopīs; rūḍha and adhirūḍha, the latter with modana and (in Rādhā alone) mādana.

notes: All stages lie within the goal (prema); banded B7 as gradations of the attained goal. Kṛṣṇadāsa compares them to the stages of refining sugar-cane (CC 2.23; verse to verify).

name: Vācaspati's four stages of (lower) dispassion (TV 1.15)

stages.name: yatamāna-saṃjñā
stages.description: Effort to keep the senses from engaging objects.

stages.name: vyatireka-saṃjñā
stages.description: Distinguishing which faults have been overcome and which remain.

stages.name: ekendriya-saṃjñā
stages.description: The senses no longer move toward objects; longing remains only in the mind.

stages.name: vaśīkāra-saṃjñā
stages.description: Indifference even to that mental longing — the lower dispassion of YS 1.15; higher dispassion (1.16) follows.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log). Stage names and glosses are recalled from Vācaspati's Tattvavaiśāradī on 1.15 and not checked against the text (the TV on 1.15 is not in the local corpus).

name: The Vaiśeṣika path to liberation (mokṣa)

stages.name: dharma (enjoined by the Lord's command / the Veda)
stages.description: Dharma, that from which prosperity and the highest good arise, as the source of the liberating knowledge (VS 1.1.2; Praśastapāda).

stages.name: observances and life-stages without impure intention
stages.description: Ablution, fasting, celibacy, residence with the teacher, forest-dwelling, sacrifice, giving etc., with pure intention (VS 6.2.2–5).

stages.name: yoga
stages.gloss: the mind abiding in the self
stages.description: The mind abides in the self; no pleasure or pain (VS 5.2.17).

stages.name: ātmapratyakṣa / tattvajñāna
stages.gloss: perception of the self; knowledge of the categories
stages.description: Perception of the self through a special conjunction of self and mind (VS 9.13); knowledge of the categories through similarities and dissimilarities (Praśastapāda; Upaskāra VS 1.1.4).

stages.name: vairāgya; no new merit or demerit
stages.description: With attachment and aversion gone, no new merit or demerit accrues (Praśastapāda).

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.gloss: no contact with a body, no new appearance
stages.description: When adṛṣṭa is exhausted, no contact and no new appearance — liberation, like a fire whose fuel is burnt (VS 5.2.20; Praśastapāda).

notes: Reconstructed sequence (moderate/low confidence for the Praśastapāda stages); bands are interpretive.

name: The growth of devotion (Vallabha's Bhaktivardhinī)

stages.name: bīja
stages.description: The seed of love given by grace (through the brahmasambandha).

stages.name: dṛḍhatā
stages.description: Made firm by renunciation, hearing and singing while remaining at home in service.

stages.name: prema / sneha
stages.description: Love that destroys attachment to other things.

stages.name: āsakti
stages.description: Attachment that makes the home distasteful.

stages.name: vyasana
stages.description: Absorption in Kṛṣṇa such that one cannot live without him; one is then fulfilled.

notes: Verse numbers approximate.

name: Varāha: the eight-limbed yoga

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Ten restraints.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Ten observances.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Named postures.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Breath-regulation (counts not reproduced).

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Five kinds of withdrawal.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Concentration.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation with or without qualities.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Absorption.

name: Varāha: the seven stages of knowledge

stages.name: śubhecchā
stages.description: Wish for liberation: 'why do I remain a fool?'

stages.name: vicāraṇā
stages.description: Inquiry with the scriptures and the good.

stages.name: tanumānasī
stages.description: Mind made subtle by the first two.

stages.name: sattvāpatti
stages.description: Resting in the pure Self; the knower of Brahman.

stages.name: asaṃsakti
stages.description: Unattached; the excellent knower.

stages.name: padārthabhāvanā
stages.description: Objects no longer appear; woken only by others' effort.

stages.name: turyagā
stages.description: No difference; one's own nature.

name: The Vāyavīya's five yogas and the Śaiva path of meditation (ŚiP 7.2.37-39)

stages.name: adhikāra: dispassion
stages.description: dispassion toward seen and scriptural objects

stages.name: mantra-yoga
stages.gloss: mind resting on the mantra's meaning

stages.name: mahā-yoga
stages.gloss: Śiva's own nature alone, without adjuncts

notes: The text also gives the eight (or six) limbs as the general frame, and saviṣaya→nirviṣaya meditation (7.2.39); presenting the five yogas as a sequence is itself an interpretation (the text says only that mahā-yoga is highest).

name: Hearing to nirvikalpa samādhi with eight auxiliaries (Vedāntasāra)

sources.ref: sections on the means and samādhi

stages.name: adhikāra
stages.description: purification through duties; the four means

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: determining the purport by the six marks

stages.name: manana
stages.description: reasoning in accord with the teaching

stages.name: yama–dhāraṇā
stages.description: restraint, observance, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding

stages.name: nididhyāsana / dhyāna
stages.description: flow of like ideas excluding unlike

stages.name: savikalpa-samādhi
stages.description: mode rests in Brahman, knower–known distinction remaining

stages.name: nirvikalpa-samādhi
stages.description: like salt dissolved in water; overcoming laya, vikṣepa, kaṣāya, rasāsvāda

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: abiding as Brahman with the body sustained by prārabdha

notes: Bands are interpretive; the Vedāntasāra itself treats samādhi as a means to the knowledge that liberates.

name: The way of bhakti-yoga (Rāmānuja)

stages.name: śāstra-jñāna
stages.description: Right knowledge of the self and the Lord from scripture and a teacher.

stages.name: sādhana-saptaka and varṇāśrama-dharma
stages.gloss: the seven aids and one's duties
stages.description: Purity of food, desirelessness, practice, ritual duties, virtues, and balance between dejection and elation.

stages.name: karma-yoga
stages.description: Duties done without agency, ownership or desire for fruit, as the Lord's worship.

stages.name: jñāna-yoga
stages.description: Contemplation of the self as distinct from matter.

stages.name: ātmāvalokana
stages.description: Direct experience of one's own self, fruit of the two preceding yogas.

stages.name: bhakti-yoga (dhruvānusmṛti)
stages.description: Unbroken remembrance of the Lord, repeated daily until death, reaching the vividness of seeing.

stages.name: parabhakti, parajñāna, paramabhakti
stages.description: Longing, vision, and love that cannot bear loss of the vision.

stages.name: utkrānti and arcirādi
stages.gloss: departure and the path of light
stages.description: At death, departure through the head channel and journey by the path of light.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Manifestation of one's own nature and enjoyment of the whole Brahman.

stages.name: nitya-kainkarya
stages.description: Eternal service of the Lord with Śrī in all places and times.

notes: Bands are interpretive (interpretation layer). The tradition itself does not number these stages; the sequence is assembled from Rāmānuja's works.

name: Keśidhvaja's yoga (VP 6.7)

stages.name: yama
stages.description: celibacy, non-harming, truth, non-stealing, non-possession, practised without desire

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: study, purity, contentment, austerity, mind turned to Brahman

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: a posture such as bhadrāsana

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: with a support (sabīja) or without (abīja)

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: the senses made to follow the mind

stages.name: dhāraṇā on śubhāśraya
stages.description: the mind fixed on Viṣṇu's form, simplified stage by stage until steady in all activities

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: one continuous flow of that form, desiring nothing else

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: grasping the object's own nature free of imagination

stages.name: brahma-prāpti / abheda
stages.description: knowledge leads the self to Brahman and ceases; difference, made by ignorance, is gone

notes: VP 6.7.33 also distinguishes the practiser (yuñjāna) from one of perfected samādhi (liberated in this birth).

name: Vyāsa's four kinds of yogin (YBh 3.51)

stages.name: prāthamakalpika
stages.description: The practising beginner in whom the light has only begun to shine.

stages.name: madhubhūmika
stages.description: Whose insight is truth-bearing (ṛtambharā); the celestials invite him and he must avoid attachment and pride.

stages.name: prajñājyotis
stages.description: Has mastered the elements and senses, guards what has been cultivated and strives for what remains to be accomplished.

stages.name: atikrāntabhāvanīya
stages.gloss: one beyond what is to be cultivated
stages.description: Whose sole aim is the dissolution of the mind; he has the sevenfold final insight.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log).

name: The five means of YS 1.20 as a sequence (YBh 1.20)

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: Serenity of mind that protects the yogin like a mother.

stages.name: vīrya
stages.description: Arises in one who has faith and seeks discrimination.

stages.name: smṛti
stages.description: Stands ready in one with energy.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: With mindfulness present the undisturbed mind is concentrated.

stages.name: prajñā(-viveka)
stages.description: By which one knows things as they are.

stages.name: asaṃprajñāta samādhi
stages.description: From practising that insight and dispassion toward its objects.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log).

name: The final sequence of the Kaivalya-pāda (YS 4.25–34)

stages.name: ātmabhāva-bhāvanā-nivṛtti
stages.gloss: cessation of speculation on the self
stages.description: For one who sees the distinction (4.25).

stages.name: viveka-nimna citta
stages.description: Borne toward kaivalya (4.26); other cognitions in its gaps are removed like afflictions (4.27–28).

stages.name: dharmamegha samādhi
stages.description: For one without interest even in the highest reflection (4.29).

stages.name: kleśa-karma-nivṛtti
stages.description: Vyāsa: the wise one is liberated while living (4.30, YBh 4.30).

stages.name: jñānānantya
stages.description: What remains to be known is little (4.31).

stages.name: pariṇāma-krama-samāpti
stages.description: Their purpose accomplished (4.32).

stages.name: kaivalya
stages.description: The guṇas return to their source; the power of consciousness is established in its own form (4.34).

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log). B8 (activity after liberation) is not assigned: the Yoga texts do not describe the liberated yogin's activity beyond YBh 4.30's 'liberated while living'; dharmamegha is placed at B6, not at the B8 example given in data_model.md, because in Yoga it precedes the cessation of afflictions and kaivalya.

name: The sevenfold final insight (YS 2.27 with YBh)

stages.name: parijñātaṃ heyam
stages.gloss: what is to be avoided is known
stages.description: Nothing more to know.

stages.name: kṣīṇā heyahetavaḥ
stages.description: Nothing more to exhaust.

stages.name: sākṣātkṛtaṃ hānam
stages.description: Through the samādhi of stilling.

stages.name: bhāvito hānopāyaḥ
stages.description: Discriminative discernment developed. (1–4: release regarding what is to be done.)

stages.name: caritādhikārā buddhiḥ
stages.description: First of the three releases of the mind.

stages.name: guṇānāṃ pralaya
stages.description: Like rocks fallen from a peak, the guṇas incline to dissolution in their cause and do not arise again.

stages.name: kevalī puruṣaḥ
stages.description: Beyond relation to the guṇas, the light of its own form alone, stainless; he is called 'skilled' (kuśala).

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U10 (see interpretation_log).

name: Yoga Yājñavalkya: the eight limbs
notes: Chapter refs recalled with low confidence. The text's samādhi is described as union of individual and supreme self and leads to liberation; banded B4 with that caveat.

name: Yogacūḍāmaṇi: the twelvefold ladder

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Twelve prāṇāyāmas make one pratyāhāra.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Twelve pratyāhāras make one dhāraṇā.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Twelve dhāraṇās make one dhyāna.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Twelve dhyānas make one samādhi.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: The culmination.

name: The Yogadīpikā's graded disciplines

stages.name: śauca, āsana, prāṇāyāma, aparigraha, ahiṃsā, satya, asteya, brahmacarya, tapas, tuṣṭi
stages.gloss: purity, posture, breath, restraints and observances
stages.description: Listed first, of least weight.

stages.name: yajña and other duties, svādhyāya, hari-arcana
stages.description: Of greater weight.

stages.name: śravaṇa, manana
stages.description: Never to be reduced.

stages.name: vyākhyāna of the Upaniṣads, bhakti
stages.description: Of the greatest weight.

notes: The text ranks these disciplines in ascending importance ('each later one with special weight'); it does not present them as successive stages. Reading them as a path map is interpretive.

name: The four stages of yoga (Yogatattva; Varāha)

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: Purification of channels; signs of lightness and fire; praṇava-japa completes it; in the Varāha, outer rites set aside and inner performed.

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: Prāṇa and apāna, mind and intellect, jīva and supreme become one; withdrawal.

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: Kuṇḍalinī enters the suṣumnā; the element concentrations.

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: Samādhi; natural yoga; liberation while living.

name: The four yogas as a sequence (Yogatattva; Yogaśikhā)

stages.name: mantra-yoga
stages.description: Repetition; in the Yogaśikhā the natural haṃsa reversed as so'ham.

stages.name: laya-yoga
stages.description: Dissolving the mind in the Lord in all activities.

stages.name: haṭha-yoga
stages.description: Eight limbs with mudrās; union of sun (ha) and moon (ṭha).

stages.name: rāja-yoga
stages.description: Gives discrimination and dispassion; union of rajas and retas.

name: The three kinds of worship (Yoginīhṛdaya)

stages.name: aparā pūjā
stages.description: Worship of the Śrīcakra and its enclosure deities, done even by Śiva, because it produces the conviction of non-difference.

stages.name: parāparā pūjā
stages.description: Meditative worship dissolving the outer into the inner non-dual abode of consciousness.

stages.name: parā pūjā
stages.description: Abiding in non-duality across every outflow of the senses: 'wherever the mind goes, there is the supreme state'.

notes: The text names the three in the order parā, aparā, parāparā; the ascending order here follows the Dīpikā's grading (aparā lowest, parā highest). Knowing this code makes one liberated while living (YH 3.1).
